A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research, renamed from ASFT to INRFlow, with matching authors, core formulation and benchmark results. Text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original image and point-cloud generation results, architectural and scaling experiments, and resolution-generalization analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds protein-folding predictions, quantitative protein evaluation and a spatial-latent ablation.

M1.justification: The PerceiverIO-based architecture and conditionally independent flow-matching framework remain. The protein adaptation adds atom, graph-Laplacian and ESM features with amino-acid-based latent aggregation. Section 3.3 also revises the written velocity target; the PDFs do not establish that implementations underlying retained benchmark results changed.

E1.justification: v2 adds sequence-conditioned protein folding on SwissProt using AlphaFold Database reference structures, extending coverage beyond images and object point clouds. Existing image datasets, Objaverse and ShapeNet remain; ShapeNet moves to Appendix F rather than being removed.

E2.justification: Appendix G/Table 13 adds an evaluated comparison against Boltz-1 for protein folding. AlphaFold3 is discussed but is not a separate reported comparator. Existing image, ShapeNet, Objaverse and interpolation comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a protein protocol with 10,000 training structures, 512 randomly selected test proteins, Cα-LDDT/TM-score metrics, and an XL model trained for 100,000 iterations at batch size 256. The new latent-placement ablation uses 200,000 steps and batch size 128. v1 specifies 1,000 SDE steps generally for point clouds; v2 specifies 500 Euler-Maruyama steps for Objaverse. v2's main-table training-cost entries conflict with its appendix, so they do not establish actual budget reductions.

E4.justification: Appendix D/Table 9 adds a focused LSUN-Church-256 ablation comparing grid, random and KMeans++ pseudo-coordinates, including increased latent count. Existing architecture, scaling, compute and resolution analyses remain, often relocated. Table 9's protein-folding caption is erroneous; its surrounding text and FID metrics identify the image experiment.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-training-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests or comparable uncertainty estimates. The shared-noise-seed approach for resolution examples is retained; new dataset sample counts do not constitute uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds protein results: Table 13 reports INRFlow Cα-LDDT/TM-score of 0.722/0.664 versus Boltz-1's 0.923/0.812. Table 9 adds latent-placement results, including FID 9.74 for grid coordinates versus 17.99 for random coordinates with 1,024 latents. Protein visualizations and additional resolution examples expand qualitative evidence. Shared benchmark scores are retained, including ImageNet-256 FID 3.74 and Objaverse ULIP-I/P-FID 0.2976/0.3638; these are not new performance gains.

T1.justification: v1 Equation 5 defines the velocity target as (1-t)*epsilon+t*y_f. v2 Section 3.3 replaces it with (epsilon-y_ft)/(1-t), consistent with the derivative of the stated linear interpolation. This is a substantive but localized mathematical correction. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion extend the explicit empirical applicability claims to protein folding and foreground the probabilistic-INR interpretation. The central contributions—single-stage ambient-space generation, a conditionally independent objective, subsampling efficiency and variable-resolution inference—remain.

C2.justification: v2 attributes poorer random-coordinate performance to uneven work across latents and discusses clustering or additional latents as remedies. It interprets protein results as encouraging despite specialized competition and notes that protein hyperparameters were not optimized. v1's optimization-difficulty explanation for degradation with dense decoding is removed, although the corresponding plot remains.

D1.justification: Appendix A.3/Table 8 document protein feature definitions, graph-Laplacian inputs and ESM-650M embeddings. Appendix H newly explains fixed encoder-resolution grid subsampling during higher-resolution decoding, and Appendix A.2 discloses 10% image-conditioning dropout. Conversely, v2 omits v1's explicit multi-level decoder/AdaLN descriptions and default decoded-pair counts. These substantially change reproducibility documentation without establishing removal of those components.

R1.justification: The existing function-space and diffusion positioning largely remains. v2 adds protein-related positioning and citations, including AlphaFold, AlphaFold3, Boltz-1 and conformer-generation work, plus references on diffusion autoencoders and efficient training. Its stronger emphasis on INRs develops a connection already present in v1.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled and ASFT is renamed throughout. The introduction is rewritten around domain-specific inductive biases and INRs. Image experiments are merged, ShapeNet and scaling discussions move to appendices, and quantitative resolution evaluation moves into the main text. The appendix structure is extensively reorganized and an impact statement is added.

P2.justification: v2 switches from single-column preprint formatting to a two-column conference layout. Figure 1 is rebuilt, protein visualizations and a resolution-sampling diagram are added, and the original scaling figure is split and relocated. Table 3 gains resource and domain-agnostic columns; new feature, ablation and protein-result tables appear. Existing sample galleries are condensed.

improvement.justification: The corrected velocity formula, protein comparison, latent-placement ablation and explicit resolution-sampling instructions improve correctness, empirical support and reproducibility. The net gain is tempered by omitted decoder details and new reporting errors: Table 3 lists 780M training examples processed for INRFlow versus 870M in Table 7, and Table 9 has an incorrect protein-folding caption. Existing benchmark performance remains unchanged.
